scenes.title: A mysterious rattle
scenes.action: Show the actual SoHelpMe opening screen.
scenes.text: Your refrigerator has picked up a new hobby: percussion. Let's use SoHelpMe to work through an unfamiliar rattle, one observation at a time.

scenes.title: Describe the problem
scenes.action: Type the refrigerator description into the real application.
scenes.text: I describe the intermittent rattling and mention that the refrigerator still seems cold. Plain language is enough. I don't need to know the name of a single refrigerator part.

scenes.title: Get help
scenes.action: Submit Get help and wait for the real response.
scenes.text: Now I choose Get help. SoHelpMe responds with a practical first check and asks for more information, instead of expecting me to arrive with a diagnosis.

scenes.title: Read the first check
scenes.action: Keep the actual response readable on screen.
scenes.text: Here, the response points to items that may be touching or vibrating, and asks what changes the rattle. I can read the suggestion and answer what I actually notice.

scenes.title: Answer with an observation
scenes.action: Report the example observation about bottles touching, then send.
scenes.text: For this demonstration, I report that two glass bottles were touching inside the door. Separating them stopped the rattle, and the refrigerator is still cooling normally.

scenes.title: A useful next step
scenes.action: Show the real follow-up response. Narrate only if the on-screen response matches.
scenes.text: The follow-up recommends keeping the bottles apart and monitoring whether the sound returns. That's a useful next step for this example, with room to continue if the problem changes.

scenes.title: Closing
scenes.action: Leave the guidance visible through the closing line.
scenes.text: A clearer description, a useful question, and a practical next step. SoHelpMe. A little help when you need it.
